findings.title: XSS Vulnerability in Dalgona Challenges - /page endpoint
findings.description: The /page endpoint reflects user input from the 'name' POST parameter into a JavaScript context without proper sanitization. The input is reflected inside a script tag: var name = "INPUT"; document.write('Hello ' + name); This allows for XSS attacks by breaking out of the string context. The application has a character-based filter that blocks certain characters (all lowercase letters, some uppercase), but the filter can potentially be bypassed using JSFuck encoding (using only []()!+ characters) or double URL encoding.
findings.evidence: POST name parameter reflected in script context: var name = "INPUT"; document.write('Hello ' + name). Filter blocks individual characters but still reflects input in textarea. XSS payload structure confirmed: ";alert('XSS');// breaks out of string context. Target server became unresponsive during testing - CTF challenge container stopped.
